description: A toy store sells plush toys and dolls. Each plush toy costs the store $3 and each doll costs the store $2. The store owner can spend at most $700 on inventory. Each plush toy is then sold for a profit of $4 while each doll is sold for a profit of $2. The owner estimates that at least 90 plush toys but at most 190 plush toys are sold each month. He also estimates that the number of dolls sold is at most twice the amount of plush toys sold. How many of each should be bought and sold to maximize profit?

CostPlushToy.definition: Cost to the store for one plush toy

CostDoll.definition: Cost to the store for one doll

ProfitPlushToy.definition: Profit earned per plush toy sold

MinPlushSold.definition: Minimum number of plush toys sold each month

MaxPlushSold.definition: Maximum number of plush toys sold each month

MaxDollToPlushRatio.definition: Maximum ratio of number of dolls sold to number of plush toys sold

objective.description: "Maximize the total profit earned from selling plush toys and dolls"

constraints.description: Total inventory cost for plush toys and dolls should not exceed the budget: 3 * (number of plush toys) + 2 * (number of dolls) ≤ 700
Number of plush toys sold must be between 90 and 190: 90 ≤ number of plush toys ≤ 190
The number of dolls sold cannot exceed twice the number of plush toys sold: number of dolls ≤ 2 * (number of plush toys)
Number of dolls must be non-negative: number of dolls ≥ 0

PlushToys.definition: Number of plush toys bought and sold

Dolls.definition: Number of dolls bought and sold
